implementation_notes: Actix Web names both roles: a handler is any async fn whose return type implements actix_web::Responder - the framework calls respond_to() to turn the value into an HttpResponse - and #[get("/users/{id}")] or web::resource registers one handler per route. The Action collects input through extractors (web::Path, web::Json), the Responder is the returned value (String, HttpResponse, or Result<T, E> coerced into an error response). The domain must be a plain async function or struct with no actix types; a custom Responder impl is worth it only when one action must produce several formats.
pitfalls: Holding a non-Send guard (for example a std MutexGuard) across an await can violate the surrounding runtime's future bounds or hold a lock across I/O -> drop the guard before awaiting or use an async-aware lock.
Extractor failures are answered by the framework before the handler runs, so their error shape differs from your own responses unless you install a custom error handler.
web::Data is an Arc: shared mutable state needs interior mutability (Mutex/RwLock) or it cannot be shared between workers.

variants.name: axum handler returning impl IntoResponse
variants.implementation_notes: axum builds on the tower/hyper stack instead of actix's own runtime: Router::new().route("/users/{id}", get(handler)) registers one handler per route and the Responder role is the IntoResponse trait - tuples like (StatusCode, Json<T>) and Result<T, E> convert into a Response. The ADR shape is identical; what differs is the extractor set (Path, State, Json), the ecosystem, and the fact that tower middleware, not framework-specific extractors, carries cross-cutting concerns.
pitfalls: Handlers must satisfy the Handler trait: an extractor that consumes the body (Json) must be the last argument or the handler fails to compile.
State<T> must be Clone and is shared across tasks, so mutable state needs Arc<Mutex<..>> or interior mutability.
Returning impl IntoResponse hides the concrete response type; keep the convention consistent across handlers or name Response explicitly.
